svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.aria-label: The public status page of Project Aether and its one-way data path. On the cloud host, a public-feed container queries Prometheus every five minutes and builds summary.json: counts, capacity gauges, short charts as plain numbers, and image tags, never host names, addresses or ports. A deny-pattern check blocks any summary that leaks one, and the last good copy goes stale instead. tsdproxy serves the file on the private mesh to the probe role only. The edge VM, through its single grant, pulls the file server-side into Glance, which draws every chart itself and escapes every value, and adds a backups list from its own Uptime Kuma. Glance is published through a cloudflared tunnel opened from inside to Cloudflare, and visitors read the page. Uptime Kuma alerts the owner on Telegram when the feed is more than 15 minutes old. Nothing flows back: the edge cannot reach the admin tools, the cluster or the hypervisor.
svg.text: One sanitised file leaves the cloud host. The edge pulls it, draws the page, and nothing flows back.

The edge has one grant into the cloud host: the probe role, over HTTPS.
Grafana, Prometheus and the admin tools don't even resolve from it.
No path from the edge, or from a visitor, to the cluster or the hypervisor.
Taking over the edge VM yields the same summary the page already shows.
A summary that fails the check is never served.
Older than 15 minutes, the page says "Data delayed"
and Uptime Kuma alerts the owner on Telegram.
The page never shows numbers it can't vouch for.
